Intake notes:

- Form version 1 requires: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country.
- Source fields use aliases: customer → cust; quantity → qty. Normalize these before submission.
- Invalid/missing priority and ship_country are the recurring rejection causes.
- A record with both fields corrected was accepted on attempt 2 (ORD-5101 and ORD-5103), so validate both explicitly before submitting.
- Correcting only one field is insufficient: ORD-5105 still failed on priority; later retries may again report both fields invalid.
- Do not rely on front-desk descriptions (“ordinary priority,” “duplicate check done,” etc.) as proof that fields are valid; inspect and normalize the actual source record.
- Verify priority against the accepted schema/value set and ensure ship_country is present and valid.
- Repeated source records represent retries of the same order; track the attempt count and avoid unnecessary duplicate submissions.
- Three failed attempts send the record to manual review; ORD-5104/5105/5106 and ORD-5107/5108/5109 reached that state.

Intake notes:

- Form versions 1–3 observed so far require the same fields: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country.
- Normalize aliases before submission: customer → cust; quantity → qty.
- Validate all three recurring problem fields explicitly: priority, qty, and ship_country. Recent records repeatedly failed on qty and ship_country, sometimes also priority.
- Do not trust front-desk descriptions (“ordinary priority,” “customer confirmed,” “duplicate check done”) as evidence of valid source values. Inspect, normalize, and validate the actual record.
- Verify priority against the accepted schema/value set; ensure qty is present, numeric/otherwise schema-valid, and correctly mapped; ensure ship_country is present and valid.
- Correcting only one field is insufficient. A record can continue failing when qty or ship_country remains invalid, even if priority is corrected.
- Repeated source details across differently numbered batches indicate retries of the same order. Track attempt count and avoid duplicate submissions.
- Three failed attempts send the record to manual review; recent sequences ORD-5110–5112, ORD-5113–5115, and ORD-5116–5118 confirm this.
- When the same source record reappears, preserve prior validation findings and fix every reported invalid field before the next attempt.

Intake notes:

- Versions 1–3 use: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country. Version 4 uses date instead of order_date; normalize date → order_date before submission.
- Normalize aliases: customer → cust; quantity → qty; date → order_date. Do not assume date formatting is accepted: normalize formats such as MM/DD/YYYY to the schema’s required format.
- Validate every required field against the actual accepted schema/value set, especially priority, qty, ship_country, and now order_date. Numeric-looking qty can still be rejected if mapping, presence, or schema validation is wrong.
- Do not trust front-desk claims (“ordinary priority,” “duplicate check done,” “confirmation email,” etc.). Inspect, normalize, and validate source values directly.
- Correct all reported invalid fields before retrying. Fixing priority alone is insufficient; recent records also retained invalid ship_country, qty, or order_date across attempts.
- Repeated customer/email/order details across batch numbers indicate retries of one source order, even when forwarded by different staff or descriptions differ. Preserve prior findings, track attempt count, and avoid duplicate submissions.
- Three failed attempts send the record to manual review. Confirmed sequences include ORD-5110–5112, ORD-5113–5115, ORD-5116–5118, ORD-5120–5121 (with the third attempt at ORD-5121), ORD-5122–5124, and ORD-5125–5127.
- Handwritten, partner-portal, and other intake origins do not establish validity; apply the same normalization and validation checks.
- When an attempt reveals invalid fields, retain those findings for the next attempt and recheck the complete record, not only the newly mentioned fields.

Intake notes:

- Normalize aliases before submission: customer/buyer → cust; quantity → qty; date → order_date. Version 4 and 5 forms use date, but the submission schema still expects order_date.
- Do not assume date formatting is accepted. Validate against the actual schema/value set; both MM/DD/YYYY and ISO-formatted dates have appeared in rejected records.
- Validate every required field and permitted value, especially priority, qty, ship_country, and order_date. Numeric-looking quantities (including 10, 73, 79, 104, 114) may still be invalid due to mapping, range, presence, or schema rules.
- Front-desk statements about duplicate checks, confirmation emails, or “ordinary” priority are not validation. Inspect and normalize source values directly.
- After any rejection, correct every reported field and recheck the complete normalized record, not just the newly mentioned fields. Retain invalid-field findings across retries.
- Repeated customer/email/order details across batch numbers identify retries of one source order, despite different staff, descriptions, or form versions. Track attempts and never create duplicate submissions.
- Confirmed retry groups now include ORD-5110–5112, 5113–5115, 5116–5118, 5120–5121, 5122–5124, 5125–5127, 5131–5133, 5134–5136, and 5137–5139. Three failed attempts send the record to manual review.
- ORD-5130 was already attempt 3 and went to manual review. Handwritten, partner-portal, and other origins do not establish validity; apply identical checks.

Intake notes:

- Normalize aliases before submission: customer/buyer → cust; quantity → qty; date → order_date. Version 4–7 forms use “date,” but the submission schema expects order_date.
- Do not assume date formatting is accepted. Validate against the actual schema/value set; ISO dates and MM/DD/YYYY dates have both been rejected.
- Validate every required field and permitted value, especially priority, qty, ship_country, and order_date. Numeric-looking quantities—including 9, 10, 11, 21, 73, 79, 90, 104, 114, and 116—may still be invalid due to mapping, range, presence, or schema rules.
- Priority labels and numbers are not interchangeable or presumptively valid: “normal,” “low,” 1, and 2 were all rejected in recent attempts. Front-desk descriptions such as “ordinary priority” are not validation.
- Version 6 and 7 submissions still require the same complete normalization and schema checks; changing form version or date format did not resolve errors.
- After any rejection, correct every reported field and recheck the complete normalized record, not just newly mentioned fields. Retain invalid-field findings across retries; repeated invalidity of buyer/cust, date/order_date, priority, qty, and ship_country indicates the whole record needs reconstruction, not isolated edits.
- Repeated customer/email/order details across batch numbers identify retries of one source order, despite different staff, descriptions, origins, or form versions. Track attempts and never create duplicate submissions.
- Confirmed retry groups: ORD-5110–5112, 5113–5115, 5116–5118, 5120–5121, 5122–5124, 5125–5127, 5131–5133, 5134–5136, 5137–5139, 5140–5142, 5143–5145, and 5146–5148. Three failed attempts send the record to manual review.
- ORD-5130 and ORD-5140–5148 (grouped above) reached manual review where applicable. Handwritten, partner-portal, and staff claims do not establish validity; apply identical checks.

Intake notes:

- Normalize aliases before submission: customer/buyer → cust; quantity → qty; date → order_date. Version 4–7 forms use “date,” but the schema expects order_date.
- Do not assume date formatting is accepted. Validate against the actual schema/value set; ISO, MM/DD/YYYY, DD/MM/YYYY, and hyphenated dates have all been rejected.
- Validate every required field and permitted value, especially cust, order_date, priority, qty, and ship_country. Numeric-looking quantities—including 9, 10, 11, 21, 73, 79, 85, 90, 104, 114, 115, and 116—may still be invalid due to mapping, range, presence, or schema rules.
- Priority labels and numbers are not interchangeable or presumptively valid: “normal,” “low,” “high,” “ordinary priority,” 0, 1, and 2 have all been rejected. Front-desk descriptions do not establish validity.
- Version 6 and 7 submissions require the same complete normalization and schema checks; changing version or date format has not resolved errors.
- After rejection, correct every reported field and recheck the complete normalized record. Repeated invalidity of cust, order_date, priority, qty, and ship_country means reconstruct the whole record, not just the newly mentioned fields.
- Repeated customer/email/order details across batch numbers identify retries of one source order, despite different staff, descriptions, origins, or versions. Track attempts and never create duplicates.
- Confirmed retry groups: ORD-5110–5112, 5113–5115, 5116–5118, 5120–5121, 5122–5124, 5125–5127, 5131–5133, 5134–5136, 5137–5139, 5140–5142, 5143–5145, 5146–5148, 5150–5151, 5152–5154, and 5155–5157. ORD-5158–5159 is an active retry group.
- Three failed attempts send a record to manual review. ORD-5130, ORD-5140–5148, ORD-5150–5157 reached manual review. Handwritten, partner-portal, staff, and customer-confirmation claims do not establish validity; apply identical checks.
